call_points.text: Broadly all of the ₹600 Cr becomes operating cash, with no depreciation, no finance cost and a ₹700 Cr tax shield of losses.
The two acquisitions add 4.5 GW and 2 GW; with 3.5 GW existing and 1.5 GW organic, management puts the total above 11 GW.
No dividend policy yet; management said the board will decide once the two acquisitions are consolidated.
Management sees limited acquisition opportunities left in India after consolidating two of the bankrupt wind OEMs.
Portfolio stands at 13+ GWp with expectations of multifold increase in consolidated EBITDA and PAT post acquisition completions.

timeline.summary: Inox Green received the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench order approving the demerger of its power evacuation business into Inox Renewable Solutions with effect from October 1, 2024.
Inox Green submitted the monitoring agency report for the preferential issue proceeds for the quarter ended March 31, 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹68.67 Cr (+0.4% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹27.79 Cr.
Inox Green reported Q4 FY26 total income of ₹120 Cr and PAT of ₹28 Cr, alongside NCLT approval for its evacuation infrastructure demerger.

Inox Green Energy Services Limited shared the audio recording of its conference call with investors/analysts held on 29th May 2026 at 17:00 hrs (IST) via inoxgreen.com/PDF/10044058_123.mp3, led by **Anup Kumar Jain**.
Inox Green's Q4FY26 call maintained FY27 EBITDA guidance above ₹600 Cr, with management saying all of it converts to operating cash and the two O&M acquisitions should consolidate in FY27.

watchlist.response: Devansh Jain disagreed, saying targets were met for 3-4 years and the FY26 shortfall was due to force majeure (shipping, ports, customer payment holds); he called the 75% FY27 guidance conservative.
watchlist.text: An investor said the company has repeatedly overcommitted and underdelivered, shifting from megawatt to revenue guidance and still falling short, with Q4 down year-on-year while peers grow over 40%.

watchlist.response: Management said one order is expected in a couple of weeks and the other in 60-90 days, with profits from 1 April 2026 reflected in FY27 consolidated results, but gave no fixed timeline.
watchlist.text: An analyst asked how the ₹600 Cr EBITDA target is reached when the 4.5 GW and 2 GW acquisitions are still awaiting NCLT clearances.

watchlist.response: Management said the ₹40 Cr is net income (about ₹25-26 Cr at PAT level) and that annualised EBITDA margin is around 50%, or about 45% excluding it.
watchlist.text: An investor asked whether the ₹40 Cr of acquisition-related other income carries associated costs and whether core margins are low without it.
